summary: Mango puffs with lemongrass coconut pudding and black sesame: puff pastry circles baked 12 minutes at 400°F, hollowed, filled with a chilled cornstarch-thickened lemongrass coconut milk pudding, a dab of black sesame paste and diced mango, and sprinkled with sesame seeds; makes 12 two-bite desserts in 1 hour (20 active).
glance: 2 1/2-inch puff pastry circles brushed with egg wash and sugar, baked 400°F about 12 minutes
one 14-ounce can coconut milk, lemongrass, sugar, 3 tablespoons cornstarch
faq: What is this dessert?
A riff on classic fruit tarts using an easy homemade coconut-milk pudding instead of pastry cream; small enough to pass at a cocktail party, with refreshing tropical flavors.
Which puff pastry should I use?

Frozen puff pastry from many grocery stores; the author prefers brands that use all butter rather than vegetable shortening. You can also make your own "rough puff" using simplified methods found on the Web.
What is black sesame paste?

Available at better Asian grocery stores, especially those specializing in Japanese ingredients: similar to tahini but thicker and sweetened and totally addictive. If you can't find it, omit it and still have a delicious dessert.
How do I make the coconut pudding?

Heat the lemongrass, coconut milk, sugar and salt near a simmer, whisk a few tablespoons into the cornstarch to form a slurry and whisk it back in, then bring to a bare simmer for one minute while whisking until it thickens, strain into a shallow bowl and chill.
How do I assemble the puffs?

Cut a circle out of the top of each baked shell leaving a 3/8-inch rim, lift off the lid, spoon in a tablespoon of pudding, 1/2 teaspoon black sesame paste, two tablespoons of diced mango and toasted black sesame seeds, and serve immediately.

summary: Cryo-pickled onions: sliced white onion and ginger sealed in a freezer bag with a rice vinegar, salt, sugar and togarashi pickling liquid, frozen at least 12 hours and thawed in the refrigerator so the pickling flavors migrate in as the water drains out; vegan, about 1/3 cup, keeps a few days.
glance: 10 minutes active plus a freeze and thaw cycle
at least 12 hours, then thaw in the refrigerator
at least a few days in the refrigerator
faq: What is cryo-pickling?

A combination the author invented of the pickling and freezing chapters in Aki Kamozawa and H. Alexander Talbot's Ideas in Food. When you freeze a vegetable, ice crystals puncture the cell walls; a slow thaw lets water drain out, giving a denser product with more concentrated flavors. Freezing and thawing in pickling liquid lets the flavors migrate in as the water goes out.
How do I make them?

Whisk the rice vinegar, salt, sugar and togarashi or chili flakes; put the thinly sliced onion (across the grain) and ginger in a small freezer bag, pour in the liquid, shake, seal forcing out as much air as possible, freeze at least 12 hours and thaw in the refrigerator.
How do I use them?
The author serves them in his pear and gouda salad, with the pickling liquid used as part of the dressing.
Can I change the vegetable or marinade?
Yes, the method is very flexible; the author suggests cantaloupe with Sichuan peppercorns.
How long do they keep?
At least a few days in the refrigerator.

summary: Crunchy-crusted yeast-raised Belgian waffles, closely based on Marion Cunningham: an overnight batter with a little rice flour for ultra-crispy surfaces and malt powder for background flavor, made in 10 minutes the night before and cooked in a Belgian-style waffle iron until quite brown; serves 4.
glance: 10 minutes the night before, then however long the waffles take
2 1/2 cups warm milk, 2 1/4 teaspoons yeast, 1 3/4 cups flour, 1/4 cup rice flour, 1/4 cup malt powder
faq: What makes a great waffle?
An ultra-crispy crust with a tender interior and some complexity of flavor, without being too sweet. The author believes there are no bad homemade waffles, only good ones and great ones.
Why add rice flour?
Rice flour is a pure starch, so it creates incredibly crunchy surfaces. The author suggests trying it in place of wheat flour for dredging in any pan-fried recipe.
What is malt powder for?
A little mysterious background flavor; Carnation malt powder can be found at many groceries.
Why use yeast and overnight batter?

Yeast delivers a great taste, and you make the batter the night before and leave it in the refrigerator; in the morning just turn on the waffle iron and ladle in the batter. Use a big bowl because the batter greatly increases in size.
How do I freeze extra waffles?
Cool them in a single layer, freeze well wrapped, and reheat in a toaster oven directly from the freezer: the original crust comes right back. The author suggests making a double batch.

summary: Buckwheat buttermilk pancakes from the Herbivoracious cookbook: half buckwheat and half all-purpose flour with buttermilk, melted butter and eggs, a fairly thick batter mixed just until combined and cooked on a medium griddle into 5-inch pancakes; makes about 12 in 20 minutes.
glance: 3/4 cup buckwheat and 3/4 cup unbleached all-purpose
faq: Why buckwheat pancakes?

Buckwheat adds a wonderfully warm, toasty, nutty flavor, but at restaurants the percentage of buckwheat flour is so low you can hardly taste it. Don't try 100% buckwheat pancakes, which are flat and taste rather sour.
How much buckwheat can I substitute?
Up to 50% buckwheat flour in any pancake recipe will be fine but possibly a little flat. Buttermilk counteracts that with a lot of leavening power.
Where do I find buckwheat flour?
At your local natural-foods store, often in the bulk section.
How thick should the batter be?
Fairly thick, so it has time to rise instead of spread. If too thick, add a bit more buttermilk or milk but keep it thick; if too thin, add a bit more of either flour.
How do I cook them?

Ladle batter into about 5-inch circles on a medium griddle rubbed with oil, cook until bubbles form on top and a peek underneath reveals a nice dark brown, then flip. Don't overmix or they will be tough.

summary: Spicy corn and potato stew, a New England chowder moved to New Mexico: corn blistered and set aside, potatoes cooked with garlic, shallots, New Mexico chile powder, cumin, Mexican oregano, lime juice and cinnamon, then simmered with corn and corncob broth; vegan, 30 minutes, serves 4.
glance: 4 cups kernels, blistered about 5 minutes; cobs simmered 10 minutes for a light broth
2 tablespoons New Mexico chili powder, cumin, 2 tablespoons Mexican oregano, cinnamon
faq: What is the idea?
If your New England corn chowder packed up and moved to New Mexico: a spicy (but not too hot) stew with plenty of garlic, chili powder, oregano and lime juice.
What is New Mexico chile powder?

The powder of a specific variety of pepper. The author finds individual chile powders have much more character than generic chili powder mixtures, and they're easy to find at any grocery with Mexican ingredients. In a pinch use any chili powder or grind dried chiles.
What is Mexican oregano?
It has a sweeter, more resinous flavor than the familiar European oreganos; if substituting European oregano, reduce the amount by half.
How do I make the corncob broth?
Put the cobs in a pot with enough water to cover, boil and simmer 10 minutes, then remove the cobs and strain the lightly flavored broth. If pressed for time, just use water.
How do I finish the stew?

Add the corn back with 2 1/2 cups of broth or water, simmer a few minutes until the potatoes are fully tender but not falling apart, then squeeze the remaining lime over each bowl and garnish with cilantro.

summary: Red curry paste from scratch, adapted from Ivy Manning: 6 dried New Mexico chile pods soaked 20 minutes in boiling water and blended for several minutes with toasted coriander, cumin, turmeric, ginger, red onion, garlic, lime zest and juice, lemongrass and cilantro; vegan, makes enough for 2 meals, freezes well.
glance: 6 dried New Mexico pods, stemmed, torn and soaked in 1/2 cup boiling water about 20 minutes
several minutes, scraping down, adding a little water as needed
freeze the excess for red curry delicata squash or red curry fried rice
faq: Why make curry paste from scratch?

There's nothing wrong with pre-packaged pastes, but homemade is easy and addictive, and the aroma and flavor of your curries will be at a completely different level. This version originated with Ivy Manning, changed a bit to use ingredients the author most often has on hand.
How hot is it?
If you like your curries hot, keep the chile seeds and ribs; if not, throw them out. Wear rubber gloves when tearing the pods.
How do I make it?

Soak the torn chile pieces in 1/2 cup boiling water in the blender jar for 20 minutes, toast coriander seeds 2 minutes in a dry skillet, add them and all the other ingredients and puree several minutes, scraping occasionally and adding a little water to bring it together.
Can I freeze it?
Yes. The recipe makes more than one meal needs; freeze the excess and you'll have the beginnings of two or three great dishes waiting, such as red curry delicata squash or red curry fried rice.
How do I prep the lemongrass?
Use only the tender white parts, pounded and roughly chopped.

summary: Double crust mac and cheese: rigatoni in a traditional gruyere and Parmigiano cheese sauce, split into a covered casserole (two-thirds) and a thin layer on a sheet pan (one-third), both topped with breadcrumbs and Parmesan and baked about 30 minutes at 425°F so everyone gets two crunchy crusts; serves 6.
glance: 2/3 in a buttered casserole, 1/3 on a greased sheet pan
425°F for about 30 minutes, until thoroughly golden brown
6 cups milk, a roux of 4 ounces butter and 1 cup flour, 10 ounces gruyere, 12 ounces Parmigiano, thyme
faq: What is the double crust idea?

Everyone knows the best part of mac and cheese is the crunchy top. Sally Schneider's suggestion in The Improvisational Cook is to bake half in a casserole and the rest in a thin layer on a baking sheet; each person gets a small amount of each, and great crispy crunchiness ensues.
How is this different from Schneider's recipe?

Her sauce thickens by pureeing some boiled pasta with the milk, which the author found lacked a little something (probably butter). His hybrid uses a traditional roux-based cheese sauce (a Mornay) with her double-top idea.
Can I make it ahead?
Yes, it's a great party dish because you can do it ahead; meat eaters will be as happy as vegetarians, and kids and adults equally joyous.
What variations work?

Any cheese that melts well, any pasta shape, any flavoring style, plus vegetables: spicy with hot peppers, luxurious with fresh truffles, or Greek flavors with lemon zest, oregano, roasted red peppers and romano.
How do I salt the sauce?
The author gives no specific measurement because it depends on how salty the cheese is; taste and adjust after stirring in the cheeses a handful at a time.

summary: French lentil salad with Latin-American flavors: French green lentils simmered about 25 minutes, tossed with roasted tiny potatoes, cucumber, radish, red onion, mint and parsley, dressed by eye with lime juice and olive oil and topped with queso fresco and avocado; serves 4 as a main or 8 as a side.
glance: 4 as a main, 8 as a side dish
1 1/2 cups French green (lentils de Puy), boiled about 25 minutes until tender but intact
start with the juice of 1 lime and a good glug of olive oil
refrigerate a day or two; serve at room temperature
yield: 4 as a main, 8 as a side dish
faq: Why French lentils?

The best, from the Puy area, are a little smaller and rounder than normal brown lentils and hold their shape even when tender instead of pureeing into lentil soup. Black beluga lentils are another option.
Why did lentil salad get a bad reputation?
It went through bad years in the 80s and 90s, usually flaccid and overdressed and filled with canned vegetables, but there's a good, simple, rustic dish underneath.
How do I dress the salad?
By eye and taste: start with the juice of 1 lime and a good glug of olive oil and toss. You've got it right when there's a slight gloss of dressing but it isn't swimming; adjust acidity and salt.
Can I change the flavors?

Use lemon instead of lime and feta instead of queso fresco, add thyme and oregano and call it Greek. Pick any combination of cooked and raw vegetables, fresh herbs and a straightforward citrus and olive oil dressing.
Can I make it ahead?
Yes, refrigerate for a day or two and bring back to room temperature or slightly warmer before serving; add the avocado and cheese at serving.

summary: Corn cake with Camembert, cherries and white honey, a sweet-savory plate: ultra-fine polenta cooked with a rosemary sprig, brown sugar and butter, molded, chilled and pan-fried crisp, served with Bing cherries, a cherry juice and sour cherry vinegar reduction, Camembert, Hawaiian white honey and flaky salt; serves 4.
glance: 2/3 cup ultra-fine polenta, 2 cups water, rosemary, 1/4 cup brown sugar, butter; set in ring molds
1/2 cup fresh cherry juice and 1/4 cup sour cherry vinegar, reduced by half
28 halved pitted cherries, 4 rounds of Camembert, 6 teaspoons white honey
faq: What is the idea?

The author started thinking of a cheese course with cherries, and it became an ambiguous sweet/savory dish he finds appealing: a corn cake that reminded him of Indian suji halva, Pacific Northwest Camembert, Bing cherries, a cherry-vinegar sauce and white honey.
What is white honey?

An unusual product from the Big Island of Hawaii, from bees that fertilize rare kiawe trees. It's raw and unfiltered with a creamy consistency like softened butter, with an intense but clean flavor, not overly floral, maybe a bit like an ice wine.
How do I make the corn cake?

Simmer a rosemary sprig in 2 cups of boiling water for 1 minute, remove it, add the ultra-fine polenta (the author used de la Estancia), brown sugar, butter and salt and simmer a couple of minutes, divide among buttered ring molds and refrigerate on parchment.
How do I finish the cakes?

Unmold and fry at high heat in a bit of oil to create a crisp crust on both sides, then serve each with cherries, 1.5 tablespoons of sauce, a piece of Camembert, 1.5 teaspoons of honey and a pinch of flaky salt.
Where do the cherries come from?
Cherries are in full storm in the Northwest in season; the author mostly eats them out of hand by the pint.

summary: Coconut rice: jasmine or basmati rice cooked in a can of coconut milk plus 1/4 cup extra water and finished with 3/4 cup of dry-toasted unsweetened shredded coconut and salt; about two minutes more work than plain rice, serves 4 as a side.
glance: 1.5 cups jasmine or basmati, cooked with one 14-ounce can coconut milk in place of an equal amount of water, plus 1/4 cup more water
3/4 cup unsweetened dried shredded, toasted about 5 minutes
faq: Why make coconut rice?

If you like coconut, it's a killer side dish: about two minutes more work than normal rice, and the rice goes from neutral canvas to stealing the show. It uses both coconut milk and unsweetened dried coconut for very intense flavor and an unexpected texture.
How do I make it?

Prepare the rice your usual way (rice cooker or stovetop) but substitute the coconut milk for an equal amount of water, then add 1/4 cup more water to make up for the coconut milk's solid content. Stir in the toasted coconut and salt just before serving, then fluff.
How do I toast the coconut?
In a dry skillet over medium-low heat (or a toaster oven), stirring frequently so it all browns nicely and none burns, about 5 minutes. Reserve a bit for garnish.
Which rice should I use?
Jasmine for a Thai or Vietnamese meal, or basmati for Indian cuisine.
How can I boost the flavor?
Add lime juice, cilantro, unrefined sugar (jaggery) or toasted black mustard seeds.
